name: Restricted Shell - Escape Techniques
description: rbash/rksh/rzsh block cd, redirection, and PATH changes but often allow command substitution and built-ins. Use backticks/$(), chaining metacharacters, and echo tricks to read files or break out.

defense.why_it_works: Restricted shells (rbash, rzsh, rksh) limit available commands and disable certain operations (cd, PATH modification, output redirection). However, they fail to restrict command substitution (backtick or $()) and metacharacters (|, ;) in some implementations, allowing escape to a full shell. Other escapes include using allowed editors (vi, ed) or language interpreters that can spawn unrestricted shells.
defense.prerequisites: Shell access as a user placed in a restricted shell. The restricted shell has an escape vector (backtick substitution, pipe metacharacter, allowed editor/interpreter that can exec shell).
defense.impact: Escape from restricted shell to a fully functional bash/sh session, enabling access to all system commands, PATH manipulation, and further privilege escalation.
defense.detection: Unexpected command execution patterns in a restricted shell session. Process audit: bash or sh process spawned from rbash parent without restricted mode. SSH session executing unusual commands.
defense.artifacts: SSH audit log (session executing commands outside restricted shell scope) | Process audit: unrestricted shell spawned from rbash
defense.prevention: Properly configure restricted shell environments. Ensure the login shell is set to rbash in /etc/passwd. Restrict allowed commands to an allowlist. Use AppArmor/SELinux profile for the restricted shell user. Ensure editors and interpreters accessible in the restricted environment cannot spawn shell processes.
defense.misconfiguration: Restricted shell configured for a user but common escape vectors left open: editors (vi, awk, python) available, backtick substitution not restricted, or $SHELL variable settable.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# /etc/passwd sets rbash
htb-user:x:1001:1001::/home/htb-user:/bin/rbash

# But vi is accessible in PATH:
# :!/bin/bash  <- shell escape from vi

# Or backtick substitution works:
ls -l `pwd`  # executes pwd outside restricted context
defense.secure_config:
# Strict rbash setup
# 1. Set login shell to rbash in /etc/passwd
# 2. Restrict PATH to controlled /home/user/bin/
# 3. Make PATH read-only: readonly PATH
# 4. Remove editors (vi, python, awk) from accessible PATH
# 5. Use ForceCommand in sshd_config for SSH sessions:
# Match User htb-user
#   ForceCommand /usr/bin/restricted-menu.sh
